basis: Official first-party pages opened and read in this session; concise original notes, not full reproductions.

sources.title: Model Spec
sources.locator: Instructions and levels of authority; The chain of command
sources.supported_takeaway: Instructions have host-defined authority; untrusted data has no instructional authority by default. Published desired behavior is not proof that a deployment always complies.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
sources.locator: Repository knowledge; Enforcing architecture; What we are still learning
sources.supported_takeaway: A navigable repository, short entry instructions, feedback tools and mechanically checked boundaries supported the reported experiment. Its architecture and permissive merge choices are not universal mandates.

sources.title: Rethinking skills and prompts for GPT-6 Astra
sources.supported_takeaway: Review accumulated prompts and skill routing for bloat and overconstraint. Define completion and safe continuation explicitly. Re-evaluate guidance for the actual model instead of extrapolating a guarantee of safe behavior.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Custom instructions with AGENTS.md
sources.supported_takeaway: Codex discovers guidance across global and project scopes. Overrides, working directory, concatenation order and byte caps affect what is loaded. Verify the actual chain rather than assuming file presence is sufficient.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Running Codex safely at OpenAI
sources.supported_takeaway: Sandbox boundaries and approval policies are different controls. Technical limits constrain access while approval policy governs escalation beyond configured authority.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Safety in building agents
sources.locator: Prompt injections; Data leakage; Best practices
sources.supported_takeaway: Treat prompt injection and private-data leakage as workflow risks. Structured intermediate data and approvals are useful defenses, not proofs of immunity. The retrieved page is product-scoped; no Agent Builder dependency is imposed here.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Guardrails - OpenAI Agents SDK
sources.supported_takeaway: Agent input/output guardrails have workflow boundaries. Parallel input checks may complete after work starts. Sensitive actions need blocking checks at the relevant tool boundary.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Function calling
sources.supported_takeaway: Tool requests and execution results form a protocol. Validate arguments and correlate results with calls; schema compliance does not grant permission to execute.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Evaluate agent workflows
sources.supported_takeaway: Evaluate workflows, not only final wording. Workflow-level testing and trace evaluation help locate failures in agent decisions and tool use.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Evaluation best practices
sources.supported_takeaway: Use representative task data, explicit criteria and repeated evaluation across changes. Separate model-assisted judging from deterministic checks and human calibration.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Sandbox security
sources.supported_takeaway: Generated code can use resources exposed to its environment. Isolate workloads, restrict networking and protect credentials independently of instructions. No hosted API is required by this package.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Conversation state
sources.supported_takeaway: Conversation continuity is an API concern with storage and context implications. Maintain durable application state separately and check the selected endpoint behavior during integration.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Reasoning best practices
sources.locator: How to prompt reasoning models effectively
sources.supported_takeaway: Clear goals, direct prompts and delimiters are preferred. Do not require private chain-of-thought disclosure. Historical endpoint-specific examples must not be applied to every newer model.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.locator: The anatomy of effective context; Long-horizon tasks
sources.supported_takeaway: Curate high-value context; retrieve information when needed; preserve relevant state across compaction. Tool ambiguity and excess instructions can reduce effectiveness.
sources.version_scope: As documented on retrieval date; installed model/host must be checked at adoption.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.locator: When and when not to use agents; Note about tooling
sources.supported_takeaway: Start with simple composable approaches and add orchestration when justified. The article itself points to newer managed-agent material for current tooling, so it is used for design principles only.

sources.title: How Claude remembers your project
sources.locator: AGENTS.md; Share one file with other coding tools
sources.supported_takeaway: CLAUDE.md and imports are supported. Current documentation also describes version- and configuration-dependent AGENTS.md loading. Verify conflicts and actual loading; do not create duplicate context files blindly.

sources.title: Configure permissions
sources.supported_takeaway: Configure permission rules and modes for the actual host. Treat instructions, approvals and operating-system isolation as distinct layers.

sources.title: Configure the sandboxed Bash tool
sources.supported_takeaway: Sandbox support and isolation behavior depend on platform and settings. Qualify file and network restrictions on the deployment operating system.

sources.title: Tool use with Claude
sources.supported_takeaway: Distinguish client-executed tools from server tools and preserve tool_use/tool_result structure and correlation. Do not translate another vendor message envelope mechanically.

sources.locator: Understand the context hierarchy; Manage context
sources.supported_takeaway: Gemini CLI has hierarchical context discovery, imports, configurable filenames and /memory inspection. Tool-triggered discovery can add more instructions later.

sources.title: Sandboxing in Gemini CLI
sources.supported_takeaway: Select and verify an isolation backend appropriate to the operating system. Approval or model steering is not itself filesystem or network isolation.

sources.title: Policy engine

sources.title: Function calling with the Gemini API
sources.supported_takeaway: Function declarations, model calls and function results use Gemini protocol structures. Validate the selected model and SDK behavior rather than relying on API compatibility assumptions.

sources.title: Thought signatures
sources.supported_takeaway: Applicable Gemini tool flows carry opaque thought signatures. Preserve provider-required protocol state without treating it as inspectable reasoning or authorization.

sources.title: Rules
sources.supported_takeaway: AGENTS.md, configured instruction paths and documented Claude-compatible fallbacks have distinct precedence. Remote instructions are a supply-chain boundary requiring trust review.

sources.title: Permissions
sources.supported_takeaway: Permission outcomes include allow, ask and deny. Pattern ordering and agent-specific overrides matter. Auto-approval settings can change the handling of ask decisions.

sources.title: Tool Calls
sources.supported_takeaway: Tool calls require client handling. Strict mode is documented as beta with endpoint and schema restrictions; do not assume OpenAI-shaped requests imply identical semantics.

sources.title: Function Calling
sources.supported_takeaway: The model proposes functions; the application executes client tools and returns correlated results. Tool choice and parallel-call settings need explicit treatment in the adapter.
